findings.title: `getClientsWithPermission` only finds the 'Clients' resource-type resource because per-client resources have no type set
findings.body: `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission(String scope)` queries `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` to find all client resources that have been granted the given scope. However, when individual client resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource(...)` (lines 104-111), `resource.setType(resourceType)` is never called—only the top-level 'all-resource' resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init(...)` has `type` set to `"Clients"`. As a result, `findByType` only ever matches the single `Clients` resource-type resource (returning `"Clients"` as a client ID in the set) and never returns the IDs of individual clients for which permissions were created. Note that `PermissionClientTest.testManageOnlyOneClient` only passes `clients().findAll()` because the caller is authenticated via `myclient`, which `ClientsResource.getClients` always includes when its own ID is in the token, masking the fact that `getClientsWithPermission` returned an empty set.

findings.title: `getResourceName` does not handle `CLIENTS` resource type
findings.body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` only has a branch for `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)` (lines 310-322) to translate the resource name (which stores the entity's internal UUID or the resource type name) into a human-readable name (`"All users"` or `user.getUsername()`). It was not updated to handle `CLIENTS.getType()`, so for client permissions it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()` (which is null/UUID rather than `"All clients"` or `client.getClientId()`), causing policy/permission representations for Clients to return raw UUIDs or null instead of clientIds.

findings.title: `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` ignores the all-clients permission when a per-client resource exists for a different scope
findings.body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)` (lines 214-224), if a resource for `client.getId()` exists in `resourceStore`, ONLY that resource is evaluated and the `Clients` resource-type resource is never checked. A per-client resource is created as soon as any permission targets that specific client (for example, a permission granting only `map-roles` on `clientA`, or a negative permission on another scope). If an administrator also has an all-clients permission granting `view` or `manage` on the `Clients` resource type, evaluating `hasPermission(clientA, VIEW)` will find the `clientA` resource, evaluate only the policies attached to `clientA` (which don't grant `view`), and return `false` instead of falling back to the `Clients` resource-type permission (compare with `UserPermissionsV2`, which evaluates both the user resource and the `Users` resource-type resource).
